name: push-growth
axis: growth by push — geometric-reallocation amortization plus the push fast path
n: N=1000000 pushes per round, ROUNDS=200 (200M pushes, each round from a fresh empty list)
nPython: N=1000000 pushes per round, ROUNDS=40 (5x fewer rounds; multiply Python's wall time by 5 to compare)
notes: Every round starts from a fresh empty list, so each round pays the full doubling schedule (~20 reallocations + copies for 1M i32). Verified on the emitted wasm that VL does NOT fuse this build into a pre-sized allocation: array.new_default + array.copy are inside the loop, so real growth is being measured. The build is consumed by summing every 64th element (~1/64 of the push cost) plus .length, which defeats dead-code elimination without diluting the axis. Scale-verified by doubling ROUNDS: vl 2.03x, rs 2.13x, js 1.93x, py 1.90x.

audit.startupFloor: Rust column is 107ms (min-of-5/7, taskset -c 2) = 6% process launcher; under the 200ms floor. Subtract the 6.8ms empty-Rust baseline before quoting a Rust:VL multiple. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
